name: GitHub
description: GitHub API integration for complete repository management including CRUD operations for repos, branches, issues, PRs, files, and more.

add_comment_to_pending_review.description: Attach another inline comment to a draft review that already exists, so a review can be built up one file at a time before being submitted. Uses GitHub's GraphQL API because the REST API only accepts inline comments when the review is first created.

path.description: File path relative to the repository root (e.g. 'src/main.py')

review_id.description: ID of the pending review to add the comment to, as returned by create_pending_pull_request_review. Omit to use the single pending review you already have open on this pull request.

line.description: Line number in the file to comment on. Must be a line that appears in the pull request diff. Omit together with subject_type FILE to comment on the file as a whole.

side.description: RIGHT for the new version (added or unchanged lines), LEFT for the old version (removed lines). Use RIGHT in almost all cases.

start_line.description: First line of a multi-line comment. Set together with line, which then acts as the last line.

start_side.description: Diff side of start_line for a multi-line comment

subject_type.description: What the comment is anchored to. Defaults to LINE; use FILE to comment on the whole file rather than a specific line.

thread_id.description: GraphQL node ID of the new review thread

review_node_id.description: GraphQL node ID of the pending review the comment was added to

add_pull_request_reviewers.description: Add reviewers to a pull request

add_reply_to_pull_request_comment.display_name: Add Reply To Pull Request Comment
add_reply_to_pull_request_comment.description: Reply to an existing inline review comment so the response threads underneath it rather than starting a new conversation on the diff.

comment_id.description: ID of the review comment being replied to. Obtain it from get_pull_request_comments.

add_sub_issue.description: Nest an existing issue underneath a parent issue to build out an issue hierarchy

issue_number.description: Number of the parent issue as shown in its URL (not the issue id)

sub_issue_id.description: The 'id' of the issue to nest — GitHub's numeric issue id, NOT its issue number. Read it from the 'id' field of a Get Issue or List Issues result. The issue must belong to the same repository owner as the parent.

replace_parent.description: Set to true to move the issue when it already has a different parent. Leave off and the request fails if it is already nested elsewhere.

cancel_workflow_run.description: Cancel a queued or in-progress workflow run to stop it consuming runner minutes

create_file.description: Create a new file in repository

create_issue_comment.description: Create a comment on an issue

create_label.description: Create a new label in a repository so it can be applied to issues and pull requests

name.description: Label name. Spaces and slashes are fine (for example 'good first issue').

color.description: Six-character hex colour code without the leading '#' (for example 'd73a4a')

description.description: Short description of the label, up to 100 characters

create_pending_pull_request_review.description: Start a draft review on a pull request without publishing it, so comments can be gathered over several steps and submitted together as one review. Nothing is visible to the author until the review is submitted.

commit_id.description: SHA of the commit the review applies to. Defaults to the most recent commit; required when posting inline comments. Obtain it from get_pull_request as head.sha.

body.description: Overall review body text, in Markdown

comments.description: Inline comments to seed the draft review with. Each must target a line that appears in the pull request diff - use get_pull_request_files or get_pull_request_diff to find valid lines. Further comments can be added later with add_comment_to_pending_review.

path.description: File path relative to the repository root (e.g. 'src/main.py')

line.description: Line number in the file to comment on. Must be present in the diff.

side.description: RIGHT for the new version (added or unchanged lines), LEFT for the old version (removed lines). Use RIGHT in almost all cases.

id.description: Review ID to pass to add_comment_to_pending_review, submit_pending_pull_request_review or delete_pending_pull_request_review

state.description: PENDING for a newly created draft

create_pull_request_review.description: Create a review for a pull request, optionally with inline comments on specific lines of changed files. Use get_pull_request first to obtain the head commit SHA (head.sha) required for commit_id.

commit_id.description: The SHA of the latest commit on the PR head branch. Required when posting inline comments. Obtain this from get_pull_request → head.sha.

body.description: Overall review body text. Required when event is REQUEST_CHANGES or COMMENT.

event.description: Review action: APPROVE, REQUEST_CHANGES, or COMMENT.

comments.description: Inline comments to post on specific lines of the diff. Each comment must target a line that actually appears in the PR diff — use diff_branch_to_branch or the patch field from get_pull_request to find valid line numbers.

path.description: File path relative to the repo root (e.g. 'src/main.py')

line.description: Line number in the file to comment on. Must be a line present in the PR diff — GitHub rejects comments on lines not in the diff.

side.description: Which side of the diff to comment on. RIGHT for the new version (added/unchanged lines), LEFT for the old version (removed lines). Use RIGHT for almost all cases.

start_line.description: First line of a multi-line comment range. Only set this when the comment spans multiple lines; omit for single-line comments.

start_side.description: Side for the start_line when making a multi-line comment. Usually matches side.

org.description: Organization name (if creating in an org)

delete_label.description: Delete a label from a repository, removing it from every issue and pull request it was applied to

delete_pending_pull_request_review.description: Discard a draft review and all of its unpublished comments. Only works while the review is still pending - a submitted review cannot be deleted.

review_id.description: ID of the pending review to discard, as returned by create_pending_pull_request_review

state.description: State of the review as it was deleted

delete_workflow_run_logs.description: Permanently delete all log files for a workflow run, for example to purge logs that captured sensitive output

download_workflow_run_artifact.display_name: Get Workflow Run Artifact Download URL
download_workflow_run_artifact.description: Resolve one artifact's download URL, size, digest and expiry. GitHub only serves artifacts as ZIP files, so this returns an authenticated download link rather than the file itself

artifact_id.description: The artifact's numeric ID, from List Workflow Run Artifacts

fork_repository.description: Create your own copy of someone else's repository, so you can push changes and open a pull request back to it. Forking runs in the background at GitHub: the fork is returned immediately but its files and branches may take a few seconds to become readable, so check the repository exists before pushing to it.

owner.description: Owner of the repository being forked

repo.description: Name of the repository being forked

organization.description: Organization to create the fork in. Defaults to the authenticated user's account.

name.description: New name for the fork. Defaults to the source repository's name.

default_branch_only.description: Fork only the default branch instead of every branch

url.description: Web URL of the new fork

source.description: The repository that was forked, as owner/name

pending.description: Always true — GitHub accepted the fork request and is still creating it in the background

get_code_quality_finding.description: Fetch one GitHub Code Quality finding with its rule, message and source location. Public preview: available on github.com only, not on GitHub Enterprise Server. Needs the repo scope and Code Quality enabled on the repository; otherwise GitHub returns 403.

finding_number.description: The finding number, as shown in GitHub and in the list action's output.

get_code_scanning_alert.description: Fetch the full detail of one code scanning alert — the rule that fired, the tool that found it and the exact file and line of the most recent occurrence. Requires GitHub Advanced Security to be enabled on the target and a token with the security_events scope; otherwise GitHub returns 403.

alert_number.description: The alert number, as shown in GitHub and in the list action's output.

get_dependabot_alert.description: Fetch one Dependabot alert with the affected package, the vulnerable version range and the first patched version, so a workflow can decide whether to open an upgrade PR. Requires GitHub Advanced Security to be enabled on the target and a token with the security_events scope; otherwise GitHub returns 403.

alert_number.description: The alert number, as shown in GitHub and in the list action's output.

get_file_content.description: Get the content of a file in a repository, or list the entries of a directory when path points to a folder. When path is a directory, 'type' is 'dir', 'content' is empty, and 'entries' holds the files and subfolders.

path.description: File path, or directory path to list its entries

type.description: 'file' for a single file, 'dir' for a directory listing

content.description: Decoded file content. Empty when path is a directory.

entries.description: Directory entries when path is a directory. Empty for a single file.

get_gist.description: Fetch one gist with the full text of every file in it, for reading a shared snippet, config or note. GitHub inlines at most 1 MB per file: when a file was cut short its 'truncated' flag is true and the whole file has to be downloaded from its raw_url, or cloned from git_pull_url once it passes 10 MB.

gist_id.description: The gist's id — the hex string at the end of its URL (e.g. '6cad326836d38bd3a7ae')

files.description: Files keyed by filename. Each holds filename, type, language, size, raw_url, truncated, content and encoding.

truncated.description: True when the file exceeded 1 MB and 'content' holds only the first part of it
True when the gist holds more than 300 files and only the first 300 are listed

git_pull_url.description: Clone URL, needed to retrieve files larger than 10 MB

get_global_security_advisory.description: Look up one advisory in the GitHub Advisory Database by GHSA ID to get its description, CVSS score, CWEs and the affected package version ranges. Needs no special scope.

ghsa_id.description: The GHSA ID of the advisory, e.g. GHSA-abcd-1234-efgh.

get_job_logs.description: Read the log output of a single workflow job as text. Job logs can run to millions of lines, so only the last tail_lines lines are returned

job_id.description: The job's numeric ID, from List Workflow Jobs

tail_lines.description: How many lines from the end of the log to return. Defaults to 500, capped at 10000

get_label.description: Look up a single label by name to check its colour and description

name.description: Label name, exactly as it appears in GitHub. Spaces and slashes are fine (for example 'good first issue').

get_latest_release.description: Get the latest published release for a repository

get_pull_request.description: Get detailed information about a pull request

head.description: The head branch info. head.sha is the latest commit SHA — pass this as commit_id when calling create_pull_request_review.

sha.description: The latest commit SHA on the PR head branch. Use as commit_id in create_pull_request_review.

get_pull_request_comments.description: List the inline review comments left on a pull request's diff, including which file and line each one is anchored to and what it replies to.

sort.description: Field to sort the comments by

direction.description: Sort direction. Defaults to ascending when sorting by created.

since.description: ISO 8601 timestamp; only return comments updated at or after this time.

limit.description: Maximum number of comments to return

max_pages.description: Maximum number of pages (100 comments per page) to fetch before stopping.

get_pull_request_diff.description: Get the complete unified diff (or git patch) for a pull request as text, so it can be read or reviewed in full without fetching each file separately.

format.description: 'diff' returns a unified diff of the whole pull request; 'patch' returns a git-format patch series with one commit message header per commit.

content.description: The raw diff or patch text

length.description: Character count of the returned text

get_pull_request_files.description: List every file a pull request touches, with its status, added/removed line counts, and per-file patch - the fastest way to see the shape of a change before reviewing it.

include_patch.description: Include the per-file patch text. Set false to get just the file list and line counts on very large pull requests.

limit.description: Maximum number of files to return

max_pages.description: Maximum number of pages (100 files per page) to fetch before stopping. GitHub itself returns at most 3000 files for a pull request.

previous_filename.description: Set when the file was renamed

status.description: added, removed, modified, renamed, copied, changed or unchanged

patch.description: Omitted by GitHub for binary files and for very large diffs

get_pull_request_reviews.description: List the reviews submitted on a pull request in chronological order, showing who approved, who requested changes, and what they said.

limit.description: Maximum number of reviews to return

max_pages.description: Maximum number of pages (100 reviews per page) to fetch before stopping.

state.description: APPROVED, CHANGES_REQUESTED, COMMENTED, DISMISSED or PENDING

submitted_at.description: Absent while a review is still PENDING

get_pull_request_status.description: Check whether a pull request's CI is passing by rolling up every commit status reported against its head commit into a single state.

sha.description: The head commit the statuses belong to

state.description: Combined state: success, pending or failure

context.description: Name of the reporting check, e.g. 'ci/circleci'

get_release.description: Get a specific release by ID

release_id.description: The unique identifier of the release

get_release_by_tag.description: Get a release by tag name

get_repository.description: Get detailed information about a repository

get_repository_tree.description: List the files and folders stored in a repository at a given branch, tag, or commit. Use recursive to walk the whole repository in one call. GitHub caps a tree at 100,000 entries / 7 MB, so always check 'truncated' — when it is true the listing is incomplete and you should read one folder at a time instead.

tree_sha.description: Branch name, tag, commit SHA, or tree SHA to read

recursive.description: Include the contents of every subfolder instead of just the top level

truncated.description: True when GitHub cut the listing short — the entries below are only part of the tree

type.description: 'blob' for a file, 'tree' for a folder, 'commit' for a submodule

size.description: File size in bytes. Absent for folders.

get_secret_scanning_alert.description: Fetch one leaked-credential alert: its type, validity, resolution and first detected location. The leaked secret itself is never requested or returned. Requires GitHub Advanced Security to be enabled on the target and a token with the security_events scope; otherwise GitHub returns 403.

alert_number.description: The alert number, as shown in GitHub and in the list action's output.

get_team_members.description: List the people on a team so you can notify them, assign reviewers, or check who has access. Members of the team's child teams are included. Note that GitHub hides private team structure: an organization or team the connected account cannot see returns a 404 rather than a permission error.

team_slug.description: The team's slug, NOT its numeric id — the URL-safe name from the team's page (github.com/orgs/<org>/teams/<team_slug>), e.g. 'platform-engineering'. Use Get Teams to look one up.

limit.description: Maximum number of members to return

get_teams.description: List the teams in an organization so you can route work, look up a team slug, or audit team structure. Omit the organization to list every team the connected account belongs to, across all of its organizations. Note that GitHub hides private team structure: if the connected account is not a member of the organization, this returns a 404 rather than a permission error, even for an organization you know exists.

org.description: Organization login (e.g. 'autohive-ai'). Omit to list the connected account's teams across every organization it belongs to.

limit.description: Maximum number of teams to return

slug.description: URL-safe team identifier; this is what team-scoped actions take, not the id

permission.description: Default repository permission granted to team members

parent.description: Parent team when this is a child team

organization.description: Owning organization login. Only returned when listing without an organization

members_count.description: Only returned when listing without an organization

repos_count.description: Only returned when listing without an organization

get_workflow_run.description: Get the full detail of one GitHub Actions run — status, conclusion, branch, commit and who triggered it

exclude_pull_requests.description: Omit the pull requests attached to the run, which makes the response smaller

get_workflow_run_logs.description: Locate a workflow run's log archive and list its jobs. GitHub only serves whole-run logs as a ZIP file, so this returns the download URL plus the job IDs you can read as text with Get Job Logs — it does not return the archive

get_workflow_run_usage.description: Get the billable runner minutes a workflow run consumed, broken down by operating system. Billable time only accrues on private repositories using GitHub-hosted runners, and excludes the macOS and Windows cost multipliers. GitHub has announced this endpoint is closing down

list_code_quality_findings.description: List GitHub Code Quality findings for a repository — maintainability and reliability issues with the rule, file and line that triggered them. Public preview: available on github.com only, not on GitHub Enterprise Server. Needs the repo scope and Code Quality enabled on the repository; otherwise GitHub returns 403.

state.description: Only return findings in this state.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100, default 100). This endpoint is cursor-paginated and does not honour page numbers, so a single request of at most 100 results is made.

list_code_scanning_alerts.description: Triage open CodeQL and third-party static-analysis alerts across a repository, or across every repository in an organization, filtered by state, severity, tool or branch. Requires GitHub Advanced Security to be enabled on the target and a token with the security_events scope; otherwise GitHub returns 403.

owner.description: Repository owner. Provide with 'repo' to scope the query to one repository.

repo.description: Repository name. Provide with 'owner' to scope the query to one repository.

org.description: Organization login. Use instead of owner/repo to scan every repository in the organization.

state.description: Only return alerts in this state.

severity.description: Only return alerts at this severity.

tool_name.description: Only return alerts raised by this analysis tool, e.g. CodeQL.

ref.description: Git reference to report on, e.g. refs/heads/main. Repository-level queries only.

pr.description: Only return alerts for this pull request number. Repository-level queries only.

sort.description: Property to sort by. Defaults to created.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-1000, default 100). Results are fetched in pages of 100.

sha.description: SHA or branch to start listing commits from

path.description: Only commits containing this file path

since.description: ISO 8601 timestamp to filter commits after

until.description: ISO 8601 timestamp to filter commits before

max_pages.description: Maximum number of pages (100 commits per page) to fetch before stopping. Prevents Lambda timeouts on large repos. Narrow with sha/path/since/until for full coverage.

list_dependabot_alerts.description: Review vulnerable dependencies flagged by Dependabot for a repository or a whole organization, filtered by state, severity, ecosystem, package or dependency scope. Requires GitHub Advanced Security to be enabled on the target and a token with the security_events scope; otherwise GitHub returns 403.

owner.description: Repository owner. Provide with 'repo' to scope the query to one repository.

repo.description: Repository name. Provide with 'owner' to scope the query to one repository.

org.description: Organization login. Use instead of owner/repo to scan every repository in the organization.

state.description: Only return alerts in this state.

severity.description: Only return alerts at this severity.

ecosystem.description: Comma-separated package ecosystems to include, e.g. npm,pip. One of composer, go, maven, npm, nuget, pip, pub, rubygems, rust.

scope.description: Only return alerts for dependencies of this scope.

manifest.description: Comma-separated manifest paths to include, e.g. package.json.

sort.description: Property to sort by. Defaults to created.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100, default 100). This endpoint is cursor-paginated and does not honour page numbers, so a single request of at most 100 results is made.

list_gists.description: List the connected account's gists, or another user's public gists, to find a snippet or track what someone has published recently. File content is not included — GitHub returns only file metadata when listing — so use Get Gist to read a file's text.

username.description: List this user's public gists. Omit to list the connected account's own gists, secret ones included.

since.description: ISO 8601 date or timestamp; only return gists updated at or after this point (e.g. '2024-01-31' or '2024-01-31T00:00:00Z')

limit.description: Maximum number of gists to return

files.description: Files keyed by filename, metadata only — no content

truncated.description: True when the gist holds more than 300 files and only the first 300 are listed

list_global_security_advisories.description: Search the public GitHub Advisory Database — for example, every critical npm advisory published this month, or the advisories affecting a specific package version. Needs no special scope.

ghsa_id.description: Return only the advisory with this GHSA ID.

cve_id.description: Return only advisories carrying this CVE ID.

ecosystem.description: Package ecosystem to filter by: actions, composer, erlang, go, maven, npm, nuget, other, pip, pub, rubygems, rust, swift.

severity.description: Only return advisories at this severity.

affects.description: Comma-separated packages, optionally pinned to a version, e.g. package1,package2@1.0.0.

published.description: Published date filter, e.g. 2024-01-01 or a 2024-01-01..2024-06-30 range.

updated.description: Last-updated date filter, e.g. >2024-01-01 or a date range.

modified.description: Published-or-updated date filter, e.g. >=2024-01-01 or a date range.

is_withdrawn.description: Set true to return only withdrawn advisories.

sort.description: Property to sort by. Defaults to published.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100, default 100). This endpoint is cursor-paginated and does not honour page numbers, so a single request of at most 100 results is made.

list_issue_fields.description: List the custom issue fields an organization has defined, including the choices available on select fields

list_issue_labels.description: List the labels currently applied to an issue or pull request

issue_number.description: Issue number as shown in the issue's URL (not the issue id)

limit.description: Maximum number of labels to return. Leave empty to return all of them.

list_issue_types.description: List the issue types an organization has defined, so issues can be classified as Bug, Feature, Task and so on

list_labels.description: List every label available in a repository, to see which labels can be applied to issues and pull requests

limit.description: Maximum number of labels to return. Leave empty to return all of them.

list_organization_repositories.description: List repositories for a specific organization

list_pull_request_commits.description: List the commits a pull request contributes, with author, committer and message - useful for writing release notes or checking commit hygiene before merging.

limit.description: Maximum number of commits to return

max_pages.description: Maximum number of pages (100 commits per page) to fetch before stopping. GitHub itself returns at most 250 commits for a pull request.

list_pull_request_reviewers.description: List reviewers for a pull request

list_pull_requests.description: List pull requests for a repository

after.description: ISO 8601 date or timestamp; keep PRs created at or after this point. A bare date (YYYY-MM-DD) is inclusive from the start of that day.

before.description: ISO 8601 date or timestamp; keep PRs created at or before this point. A bare date (YYYY-MM-DD) is inclusive through the end of that day.

limit.description: Maximum number of PRs to return

max_pages.description: Maximum number of pages (100 PRs per page) to fetch before stopping. Prevents Lambda timeouts on large repos. Narrow with state/author/after/before for full coverage.

list_repositories.description: List repositories for a user or organization

list_repository_collaborators.description: See who has access to a repository and what each person is allowed to do, so you can audit permissions or find the right reviewer.

affiliation.description: Which collaborators to include: 'direct' for people added to the repository, 'outside' for people outside the organization, 'all' for everyone visible (default)

permission.description: Only return collaborators with this permission level

limit.description: Maximum number of collaborators to return

url.description: Web URL of the collaborator's profile

role_name.description: Named role, e.g. read, triage, write, maintain, admin

list_repository_security_advisories.description: List the security advisories your team has drafted or published on a repository, or across every repository in an organization — useful for tracking embargoed advisories still in triage or draft. Needs the repo scope; organization-wide queries additionally require owner or security manager access, otherwise GitHub returns 403.

owner.description: Repository owner. Provide with 'repo' to scope the query to one repository.

repo.description: Repository name. Provide with 'owner' to scope the query to one repository.

org.description: Organization login. Use instead of owner/repo to scan every repository in the organization.

state.description: Only return advisories in this state.

sort.description: Property to sort by. Defaults to created.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-100, default 100). This endpoint is cursor-paginated and does not honour page numbers, so a single request of at most 100 results is made.

list_secret_scanning_alerts.description: Review leaked-credential alerts for a repository or a whole organization. The leaked secret itself is never requested or returned — only the alert metadata (type, state, validity and where it was found). Requires GitHub Advanced Security to be enabled on the target and a token with the security_events scope; otherwise GitHub returns 403.

owner.description: Repository owner. Provide with 'repo' to scope the query to one repository.

repo.description: Repository name. Provide with 'owner' to scope the query to one repository.

org.description: Organization login. Use instead of owner/repo to scan every repository in the organization.

state.description: Only return alerts in this state.

secret_type.description: Comma-separated secret type slugs to include, e.g. github_personal_access_token.

resolution.description: Only return resolved alerts closed for this reason.

validity.description: Comma-separated validity states to include: active, inactive, unknown. Active means GitHub confirmed the credential still works.

sort.description: Property to sort by. Defaults to created.

limit.description: Maximum number of results to return (1-1000, default 100). Results are fetched in pages of 100.

list_sub_issues.description: List the sub-issues nested under a parent issue, to see how a piece of work breaks down

issue_number.description: Number of the parent issue as shown in its URL (not the issue id)

limit.description: Maximum number of sub-issues to return. Leave empty to return all of them.

list_tags.description: List all tags for a repository

list_user_repositories.description: List repositories for a specific user or authenticated user

list_workflow_jobs.description: List the jobs in a workflow run with each job's step-by-step outcome, to pinpoint what failed

filter.description: 'latest' returns jobs from the most recent attempt only; 'all' includes every attempt

limit.description: Maximum number of jobs to return

list_workflow_run_artifacts.description: List the build artifacts a workflow run uploaded, with their sizes, expiry dates and download URLs

name.description: Return only artifacts with this exact name

limit.description: Maximum number of artifacts to return

push_files.description: Commit several files to a branch in one single commit, instead of one commit per file. Creates or overwrites each file given, and can delete files in the same commit. File content is plain text by default; set a file's encoding to base64 to push an image or other binary. If a step fails, the error says which step and whether anything was committed.

branch.description: Existing branch to commit to. The branch must already exist.

files.description: Files to create or overwrite. Each path may appear only once across files and delete_paths.

path.description: File path relative to the repository root, e.g. src/app.py

content.description: File content. Plain text unless encoding is base64.

encoding.description: How content is encoded. Defaults to utf-8; use base64 for binary files.

mode.description: Git file mode: 100644 for a normal file (default), 100755 for an executable, 120000 for a symlink

delete_paths.description: Files to delete in the same commit. Each path must already exist on the branch.

force.description: Move the branch even if the commit is not a fast-forward. Off by default; leaving it off protects work pushed by someone else while this commit was being built.

tree_sha.description: SHA of the tree the new commit points at

parent_sha.description: The commit the branch pointed at before this push

remove_pull_request_reviewers.description: Remove reviewers from a pull request

remove_sub_issue.description: Detach a sub-issue from its parent issue. The issue itself is not deleted, only the parent link.

issue_number.description: Number of the parent issue as shown in its URL (not the issue id)

sub_issue_id.description: The 'id' of the sub-issue to detach — GitHub's numeric issue id, NOT its issue number. Read it from the 'id' field of a List Sub-Issues or Get Issue result.

reprioritize_sub_issue.description: Reorder a sub-issue within its parent's list by placing it after or before another sub-issue

issue_number.description: Number of the parent issue as shown in its URL (not the issue id)

sub_issue_id.description: The 'id' of the sub-issue to move — GitHub's numeric issue id, NOT its issue number. Read it from the 'id' field of a List Sub-Issues result.

after_id.description: The 'id' (not issue number) of the sub-issue to place this one after. Supply exactly one of after_id or before_id.

before_id.description: The 'id' (not issue number) of the sub-issue to place this one before. Supply exactly one of after_id or before_id.

rerun_failed_jobs.description: Re-run only the failed jobs of a workflow run, leaving jobs that already succeeded alone

enable_debug_logging.description: Turn on runner and step debug logging for the re-run

rerun_workflow_run.description: Re-run every job in a workflow run, for example after fixing a flaky test or an expired credential

enable_debug_logging.description: Turn on runner and step debug logging for the re-run

run_workflow.description: Trigger a workflow on a branch or tag. The workflow must declare a workflow_dispatch trigger

workflow_id.description: The workflow's numeric ID or its filename, for example 'ci.yml'

ref.description: Branch or tag name to run the workflow against

inputs.description: Values for the workflow's own inputs, keyed by input name. At most 25 keys

return_run_details.description: Ask GitHub to return the new run's ID and URL. Off by default, in which case GitHub confirms the dispatch without identifying the run

search_code.description: Find source files anywhere on GitHub by their contents — locate every usage of a function, config key, or dependency across an organisation. The query must contain at least one search term (a bare 'language:go' is rejected); narrow it with qualifiers like 'repo:owner/name', 'org:acme', 'path:src/', 'language:python', 'filename:Dockerfile'. Only default branches are indexed, only files under 384 KB, and forks only when they out-star their parent. Code search is the most tightly rate limited GitHub endpoint: 10 requests per minute, and no query returns more than 1000 results.

query.description: Code search query, e.g. 'addClass org:autohive-ai language:python'. Must include at least one search term alongside any qualifiers.

sort.description: Sort field. 'indexed' orders by when the file was last indexed and is being closed down by GitHub; omit for best match.

order.description: Sort direction. Only meaningful alongside sort.

limit.description: Maximum number of files to return (GitHub caps any search at 1000).

total_count.description: Total matches GitHub found, which may exceed the 1000 results the API will return

incomplete_results.description: True when GitHub timed out and returned only part of the matches

capped.description: True when total_count exceeds the 1000-result ceiling, so items is a prefix of the matches

search_commits.description: Find commits across GitHub by message, author, or date — useful for tracing when a change landed or auditing what someone shipped. Narrow with qualifiers like 'repo:owner/name', 'org:acme', 'author:octocat', 'committer-date:>2024-01-01', 'merge:false'. Rate limited to 30 requests per minute, and no query returns more than 1000 results.

query.description: Commit search query, e.g. 'repo:octocat/Hello-World fix author:octocat'.

sort.description: Sort field for commit search. Only 'author-date' and 'committer-date' are valid here — any other value is rejected by GitHub. Omit for best match.

order.description: Sort direction. Only meaningful alongside sort.

limit.description: Maximum number of commits to return (GitHub caps any search at 1000).

total_count.description: Total matches GitHub found, which may exceed the 1000 results the API will return

incomplete_results.description: True when GitHub timed out and returned only part of the matches

capped.description: True when total_count exceeds the 1000-result ceiling, so items is a prefix of the matches

search_issues.description: Find issues across GitHub — triage everything labelled 'bug' in an org, or every issue assigned to someone across repositories. Pull requests are excluded automatically ('is:issue' is added unless the query already says which type it wants). Narrow with qualifiers like 'repo:owner/name', 'org:acme', 'author:octocat', 'assignee:octocat', 'label:bug', 'state:open', 'created:>2024-01-01'. Spaces between qualifiers combine with AND. Rate limited to 30 requests per minute, and no query returns more than 1000 results.

query.description: Issue search query, e.g. 'org:autohive-ai label:bug state:open'. 'is:issue' is appended automatically unless the query already sets the type.

sort.description: Sort field for issue search. Repository sort values such as 'stars' are rejected by GitHub here. Omit for best match.

order.description: Sort direction. Only meaningful alongside sort.

limit.description: Maximum number of issues to return (GitHub caps any search at 1000).

total_count.description: Total matches GitHub found, which may exceed the 1000 results the API will return

incomplete_results.description: True when GitHub timed out and returned only part of the matches

capped.description: True when total_count exceeds the 1000-result ceiling, so items is a prefix of the matches

search_orgs.description: Find GitHub organizations by name, description, or location. GitHub has no dedicated organization search endpoint, so this runs the account search with 'type:org' added (unless the query already sets a type) — the same index Search Users reads, filtered to organizations. Narrow with qualifiers like 'in:login', 'in:name', 'location:london', 'repos:>50'. Rate limited to 30 requests per minute, and no query returns more than 1000 results.

query.description: Organization search query, e.g. 'autohive in:name'. 'type:org' is appended automatically unless the query already sets a type.

sort.description: Sort field for account search. Only 'followers', 'repositories' and 'joined' are valid here. Omit for best match.

order.description: Sort direction. Only meaningful alongside sort.

limit.description: Maximum number of organizations to return (GitHub caps any search at 1000).

total_count.description: Total matches GitHub found, which may exceed the 1000 results the API will return

incomplete_results.description: True when GitHub timed out and returned only part of the matches

capped.description: True when total_count exceeds the 1000-result ceiling, so items is a prefix of the matches

search_pull_requests.description: Find pull requests across GitHub — review queues, everything a person opened this quarter, or every PR touching a repository. Uses the same index as issue search, with 'is:pr' added unless the query already says which type it wants. Narrow with qualifiers like 'repo:owner/name', 'org:acme', 'author:octocat', 'review-requested:octocat', 'state:open', 'draft:false', 'merged:>2024-01-01'. Spaces between qualifiers combine with AND. Rate limited to 30 requests per minute, and no query returns more than 1000 results.

query.description: Pull request search query, e.g. 'org:autohive-ai review-requested:octocat state:open'. 'is:pr' is appended automatically unless the query already sets the type.

sort.description: Sort field. Pull request search runs on the issues endpoint, so it accepts the issue sort values — not repository ones like 'stars'. Omit for best match.

order.description: Sort direction. Only meaningful alongside sort.

limit.description: Maximum number of pull requests to return (GitHub caps any search at 1000).

total_count.description: Total matches GitHub found, which may exceed the 1000 results the API will return

incomplete_results.description: True when GitHub timed out and returned only part of the matches

capped.description: True when total_count exceeds the 1000-result ceiling, so items is a prefix of the matches

search_repositories.description: Find repositories across GitHub by name, description, topic, language, or popularity — discover what an organisation owns, or shortlist libraries by stars. Narrow with qualifiers like 'org:acme', 'user:octocat', 'language:python', 'topic:cli', 'stars:>100', 'pushed:>2024-01-01', 'archived:false'. Rate limited to 30 requests per minute, and no query returns more than 1000 results.

query.description: Repository search query, e.g. 'org:autohive-ai language:python stars:>10'.

sort.description: Sort field for repository search. Only 'stars', 'forks', 'help-wanted-issues' and 'updated' are valid here — issue sort values such as 'comments' are rejected. Omit for best match.

order.description: Sort direction. Only meaningful alongside sort.

limit.description: Maximum number of repositories to return (GitHub caps any search at 1000).

total_count.description: Total matches GitHub found, which may exceed the 1000 results the API will return

incomplete_results.description: True when GitHub timed out and returned only part of the matches

capped.description: True when total_count exceeds the 1000-result ceiling, so items is a prefix of the matches

search_users.description: Find people on GitHub by username, name, email, location, or activity — for example every contributor in a city, or the account behind an email address. Organizations are filtered out ('type:user' is added unless the query already sets a type; use Search Organizations for those). Narrow with qualifiers like 'in:login', 'in:email', 'location:berlin', 'language:python', 'followers:>100', 'repos:>10'. Rate limited to 30 requests per minute, and no query returns more than 1000 results.

query.description: User search query, e.g. 'octocat in:login location:london'. 'type:user' is appended automatically unless the query already sets a type.

sort.description: Sort field for account search. Only 'followers', 'repositories' and 'joined' are valid here. Omit for best match.

order.description: Sort direction. Only meaningful alongside sort.

limit.description: Maximum number of accounts to return (GitHub caps any search at 1000).

total_count.description: Total matches GitHub found, which may exceed the 1000 results the API will return

incomplete_results.description: True when GitHub timed out and returned only part of the matches

capped.description: True when total_count exceeds the 1000-result ceiling, so items is a prefix of the matches

submit_pending_pull_request_review.description: Publish a draft review, delivering all of its inline comments at once as an approval, a change request, or a plain comment.

review_id.description: ID of the pending review to submit, as returned by create_pending_pull_request_review

event.description: How to submit the review. APPROVE and REQUEST_CHANGES cannot be used on your own pull request.

body.description: Review summary text, in Markdown. Required by GitHub when event is REQUEST_CHANGES or COMMENT and the draft has no body yet.

update_file.description: Update an existing file in repository

update_gist.description: Edit an existing gist: change its description, rewrite or rename a file, add a new file, or remove one. Only the files you name are touched; everything else in the gist is left alone. Deleting is deliberately kept separate from editing, in 'delete_files', so a malformed edit cannot destroy a file by accident.

gist_id.description: The gist's id — the hex string at the end of its URL

description.description: New description for the gist. Omit to leave it unchanged.

files.description: Files to add or change, keyed by the file's CURRENT filename. Each value is an object with 'content' (the file's new full text) and/or 'filename' (a new name, which renames the file). Use a filename that is not in the gist yet to add a file. Example: {"notes.md": {"content": "# Notes"}, "old.py": {"filename": "new.py"}}. An entry with neither key is rejected rather than sent, because GitHub would read it as a deletion.

content.description: The file's new full contents (replaces, not appends)

filename.description: New name for the file — supplying this renames it

delete_files.description: Filenames to delete from the gist. Deleting a gist's last remaining file deletes the gist itself.

files.description: The gist's files after the update, keyed by filename, metadata only

update_label.description: Rename a label or change its colour or description across every issue it is applied to

new_name.description: New name for the label. Leave empty to keep the current name.

color.description: Six-character hex colour code without the leading '#' (for example 'd73a4a')

description.description: Short description of the label, up to 100 characters

update_pull_request.description: Edit an open pull request - retitle it, rewrite its description, retarget it at a different base branch, or close/reopen it without merging.

title.description: New pull request title. Leave unset to keep the current title.

body.description: New pull request description in Markdown. Replaces the existing body entirely.

state.description: Set to 'closed' to close the pull request without merging, or 'open' to reopen it.

base.description: Name of an existing branch to retarget the pull request at (e.g. 'main'). Cannot be the same as the head branch.

maintainer_can_modify.description: Whether maintainers of the base repository may push to the head branch. Only settable on pull requests from a fork.

update_pull_request_branch.description: Bring a pull request's branch up to date with its base branch by merging the base into it - the equivalent of clicking 'Update branch' on GitHub. Useful when a branch protection rule requires branches to be current before merging.

expected_head_sha.description: The SHA the head branch is expected to be at. If the branch has moved on since, GitHub rejects the update instead of merging over someone else's push. Obtain it from get_pull_request as head.sha.

queued.description: GitHub accepted the request and runs the merge as a background job; the branch may take a moment to reflect it.
